sense: appealing: an offer, an idea, a price

evidence: Cic. de Or. 1.221: expetenda atque optābilia (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: What one would wish to have; optābile est ut, it would be ideal if.

evidence: Cic. Mil. 43: maxima est illecebra peccandi impūnitātis spēs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: A lure, in a good or a bad sense; a favourite word of Cicero’s. What makes an offer attractive is its illecebra.

terms.register: vōx cōmica: Plaut.; then late (Prud., Amm.)

phrases.latin: cuique pāx, praesertim cīvīlis, quamquam omnibus bonīs, tamen in prīmīs fuit optābilis
phrases.english: to whom peace, civil peace above all, though desirable to all good men, was more desirable than to anyone

sources: Lewis & Short: optabilis · Lewis & Short: illecebra · Lewis & Short: illecebrosus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 149.
